video_title: The LaMelo Ball Trade! | The Jon Krawczynski Show

quotes.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
quotes.summary_phrase: Timberwolves' interest in acquiring LaMelo Ball
quotes.excerpt: It started to percolate that, hey, maybe the Wolves have a little bit of interest in LaMelo Ball

text_blocks.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
text_blocks.text: It started to percolate that, hey, maybe the Wolves have a little bit of interest in LaMelo Ball and I asked you to come on and I figured, all right, we'll just talk a little bit through some of the possibilities and lo and behold, we both wake up this morning and the deal is done. It's LaMelo Ball to the Minnesota Timberwolves, Naz Reid and draft pick compensation is going out the door.

text_blocks.speaker: Dane Moore
text_blocks.text: The first time I knew it was a possibility was when you said, 'Hey, Dane, you want to come on my podcast tomorrow morning?' and I said, 'What are we going to talk about?' You said, 'LaMelo,' and I was like, 'Oh, okay, so this is happening.'

quotes.speaker: Dane Moore
quotes.summary_phrase: Impact of trading Naz Reid for LaMelo Ball
quotes.excerpt: I didn't expect the Naz Reid part of it. I think from a Timberwolves' perspective, he's the longest-tenured Timberwolf

text_blocks.speaker: Dane Moore
text_blocks.text: I didn't expect the Naz Reid part of it. I think from a Timberwolves' perspective, he's the longest-tenured Timberwolf, awesome guy, somebody that I wanted to see come into full flower, and it looked like that opportunity was going to be there without Julius Randle. So that was the first thing when I saw the Shams tweet, I was like, 'Oh, Naz, it's Naz, it's not Rudy.'

text_blocks.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
text_blocks.text: I want to spend a lot of time on Naz here in just a bit because he deserves it. He has been here through thick and thin, he has made himself into a great player, he is obviously a folk hero here in the Twin Cities, and so I am conflicted about that part of it.

quotes.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
quotes.summary_phrase: Timberwolves' long-term interest in pairing LaMelo Ball with Anthony Edwards
quotes.excerpt: Tim Connelly and Chris Finch have long believed that LaMelo Ball is a perfect fit for Anthony Edwards

text_blocks.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
text_blocks.text: I think Tim Connelly and Chris Finch have long believed that LaMelo Ball is a perfect fit for Anthony Edwards in that backcourt. And I know that over the last several years, they have checked in on LaMelo and Charlotte a couple of times. Each time they were turned away, and so something has happened in the last couple of days or weeks to get the Charlotte Hornets to a point where they were comfortable parting with LaMelo Ball.

text_blocks.speaker: Dane Moore
text_blocks.text: If the theme of this off-season thus far, from what Chris Finch and Tim Connelly have told us in press conferences, is that they want to get younger, they want the high bar of the roster age-wise to be 26 years old.

quotes.speaker: Dane Moore
quotes.summary_phrase: Timberwolves' shift to a younger roster strategy
quotes.excerpt: It's a really, really young team. I think there's only two guys on the team that are in their 30s

text_blocks.speaker: Dane Moore
text_blocks.text: It's a really, really young team. I think there's only two guys on the team that are in their 30s, Rudy and Dante DiVincenzo, who's not going to play. Also, LaMelo, three years left on his contract. Anthony Edwards, three years left on his contract. Jaden McDaniels, three years left on his contract. Nickeil Alexander-Walker, three years left on his contract. We always talked about the second window, the second window of the Anthony Edwards era, this is it.

text_blocks.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
text_blocks.text: They did get younger, but I don't think there's a question that if you want to put LaMelo Ball, Kyrie Irving coming off of a knee injury, and Ja Morant in a bucket, LaMelo Ball is the best player of the three of them right now.

quotes.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
quotes.summary_phrase: Analysis of the draft pick compensation in the LaMelo Ball trade
quotes.excerpt: The big pick is the 2033 unprotected first-round pick, and 2033 is certainly a long ways off

text_blocks.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
text_blocks.text: The big pick is the 2033 unprotected first-round pick, and 2033 is certainly a long ways off. If I'm Charlotte, I'm looking at that like that's a nice pick. That will be a nice pick, but it's seven years down the line.

text_blocks.speaker: Dane Moore
text_blocks.text: I do think from an opportunity cost standpoint, you could have maybe traded that pick so distant into the future for maybe two first-round picks more closely, and then you don't necessarily need to go all-in.

quotes.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
quotes.excerpt: They were in on Jaylen Brown as well. It was made clear by the Celtics that he was going to be available

text_blocks.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
text_blocks.text: They were in on Jaylen Brown as well. It was made clear by the Celtics that he was going to be available and the Wolves were trying to have conversations about what it would take to get Jaylen Brown. I think that they looked at those two, Jaylen Brown and LaMelo Ball, and Brown, just because he's won a championship, he's a little older, he was top-six MVP this year, I think that the Celtics were asking more for Brown than what the Hornets wanted for Ball.

text_blocks.speaker: Dane Moore
text_blocks.text: I think the functional way they could have done that trade in the same sort of way, they'd included, this is all part of the Julius Randle trade now, so in this trade, the Wolves are taking on LaMelo Ball and Josh Green, and that's like $56 million of salary.

quotes.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
quotes.summary_phrase: Timberwolves' strategy of surrounding stars with depth
quotes.excerpt: In this current NBA, you basically have 1.5 or two stars and then surround him with depth

text_blocks.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
text_blocks.text: In this current NBA, you basically have 1.5 or two stars and then surround him with depth. And that's the road map to contention anymore. There's no more three-star models, any of that. And so they are banking that LaMelo Ball will be healthy enough, which they have a very good training staff, so that's I think encouraging, and that he will be maturing from a winning decision-making standpoint to be reliable that way.

text_blocks.speaker: Dane Moore
text_blocks.text: I think there's a couple of pathways to sort of round this out a little bit just because his salary point is a little bit lower. I think they're done from a pursuing star standpoint, but this roster is also a little bit incomplete.

quotes.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
quotes.summary_phrase: Timberwolves' refusal to trade Dante DiVincenzo
quotes.excerpt: Boston was not going to take just Naz Reid and picks for Jaylen Brown

text_blocks.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
text_blocks.text: Boston was not going to take just Naz Reid and picks for Jaylen Brown. And so I think, I'm just guessing at this, but my speculation is that it would have required Rudy, Naz, and maybe even like Dante DiVincenzo or someone else and picks for Jaylen Brown, and that just was not going to be a realistic thing.

text_blocks.speaker: Dane Moore
text_blocks.text: I've heard San Mamadou Kalashvili from Toronto as potentially an option there. Now, I think that's going to depend on what his free agent market place ends up being.

quotes.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
quotes.summary_phrase: Timberwolves' commitment to keeping Dante DiVincenzo
quotes.excerpt: I was told that they do not want to trade Dante DiVincenzo still

text_blocks.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
text_blocks.text: I was told that they do not want to trade Dante DiVincenzo still. So that the plan is to keep him, rehab him, and get him back on the floor sometime this season. Plans can change, but as of right now, they do not envision trading Dante DiVincenzo.

text_blocks.speaker: Dane Moore
text_blocks.text: I've heard some of the shooter names, like I think Quentin Grimes is out there, Tim Hardaway Jr. is out there, several, you know, there are several guys like that that, you know, could come in.

quotes.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
quotes.summary_phrase: Reflecting on Naz Reid's development and legacy
quotes.excerpt: There has never been a better development story in this team's history, I don't think

text_blocks.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
text_blocks.text: There has never been a better development story in this team's history, I don't think. He comes in as this pudgy, kind of injured guy from LSU that's undrafted. You don't know, is he a five, is he a four, what can he do? And man, this guy just constantly every single year changed his body, added to his game, was completely selfless in being a sixth man behind Karl-Anthony Towns, behind Julius Randle, and over and over and again, delivered for these guys.

text_blocks.speaker: Dane Moore
text_blocks.text: I think the development story thing is the thing to focus on, not just because he is the best development story in Timberwolves history, I think part of the reason why he became such a cult hero figure here is because he was a development story.
